# Attachment Plan Functions

Builds an attachment clause’s contract and initial-state plan. `plan()` takes no arguments and returns the inherited `attachmentPlan()` result. Planning validates configuration and constructs operations, hooks and embedding declarations; it does not itself prepare, create or attach an instruction.

## Configuration

The planner reads `/clauseRuntime/work/candidate/<clauseKey>`, using the `clauseKey` constant. Its `parameters` override these defaults: `authority: "guarantor"`, `payer: "customer"`, `payee: "seller"` and `hooks: {}`.

- `type/actorParameter` selects the parameter naming the operations’ actor channel; it falls back to `payer`, whose default value is `customer`.
- `authority` must equal `type/authorityRole`.
- `template/type` is required and must have exactly the identity specified by `type/instructionType/type`. Each mapping in `type/partyFields` requires the corresponding template field to equal its named parameter.
- `type/allowedActions` limits hook action names. `type/allowCreate` enables creation only when exactly `true`. The planner also carries `type/kind`, `type/requestType/type` and `type/termsPath` into runtime constants.
- `bindings/request` defaults to `/attachmentRequest_<clauseKey>`; `bindings/instruction` defaults to `/instruction_<clauseKey>`. Both must be distinct, non-root, single-segment top-level paths. Neither may be `/activation`, `/contracts`, `/clauses`, `/clauseRuntime`, `/sources`, `/attachmentState_<clauseKey>` or `/attachmentAccess_<clauseKey>`.

`clauseKey`, the selected actor, `authority` and hook names must be nonempty text without `.`, `/`, `~` or `__`. Invalid names, conflicting paths, template mismatches and unsupported hooks reject planning.

`validateConfiguration()` returns `{allowed: true, code: ""}`; the planner’s checks still apply. `validateTransition()` returns `{allowed: false, code: "ATTACHMENT_POLICY_IMMUTABLE"}`, rejecting policy transitions through that validator.

## Hooks

`hooks` groups named hooks by allowed action. Inherited `compileHooks(allowed, hooks, key)` returns lowered `bindings`, `signals`, `parentDependencies` and a `relationship` of `one-way` or `cross-embedded`. Any parent-scoped hook selects `cross-embedded`.

A hook’s `in` defaults to `instruction`; `on` defaults to `workflow`. Instruction-scoped hooks must use `workflow`. Parent-scoped hooks must use `event` or `state`:

- `event` requires an `event` field and is lowered to an embedded hook at `/sources/parent`.
- `state` requires a `path` beginning with `/` and an `equals` field. It produces a signal identified as `<action>_<hookName>`. The lowered hook listens for `Source Changed` with the attachment key and signal identifier, then checks the parent value against `equals` together with `when`, which defaults to `true`. The signal reports a source update; it does not confirm an attachment action’s completion.

Parent hooks also require the parent’s selected instruction to have the same initialized-document identity as the executing instruction. Their generated `before` checks require `/sources/parent/activation/active` to be exactly `true`, the configured authority to appear in the parent roster, and matching primary channels and reader-key memberships for every parent party. These checks precede any supplied `before` effects.

Here, `/sources/parent`, `/activation` and `/contracts/initialized/document` belong to the executing instruction’s own document. The selected instruction is located through `/clauses/attachment/parameters/instructionPath` within the embedded parent.

Explicit `recheckOn` is allowed only for parent `state` hooks, even when its list is empty. Such hooks cannot specify `before` or `after`. Their `params` and `when`, defaulting to `{}` and `true`, must avoid `$event`, `$binding`, `$var`, `$resultValue`, `$call`, `$const`, `$steps`, `$currentContract`, `$intrinsic`, `$events` and `$changeset`; expression inspection has a 32-level traversal limit. Each recheck path must begin with `/`, differ from `/`, not begin with `/sources`, and be unique within that hook. Additional `<hookName>_recheck_<index>` hooks use `on: "change"` at those paths in the instruction document, retaining the parent-state and identity conditions. Hook-name collisions reject compilation.

## Planned operations and state

The result contains `contracts`, `reads: []` and `states/attachment`. The attachment state is an object at `/attachmentState_<clauseKey>` with initial `status: "waiting"`. This is initialization specified by the plan, not an interpretation of an absent state value. The empty `reads` list does not mean planning performs no document reads.

The `embedded` contribution declares the instruction path and the `/attachmentAccess_<clauseKey>` collection for embedded processing. Operations use the selected actor channel and pass `call/request` as their runtime `input`:

- `prepare_<clauseKey>` calls `preparePublic`. Its request accepts `values` permitted by the template and `authorityParty`, required when the configured authority is absent. If supplied for an existing authority, `authorityParty` must agree with it. `values` may be omitted when configuration requires none.
- `attach_<clauseKey>` accepts `document`, the exact publication of an existing initialized document supplied by reference. Its request description specifies runtime checks of document type, parties and admission state.
- `create_<clauseKey>` is generated only when `allowCreate` is exactly `true`; its request requires no fields and uses prepared document state.
- `addAuthority_<clauseKey>` and `registerAccess_<clauseKey>` provide the authority and access operations described below.

Preparation, attachment and creation delegate to runtime functions; generating or invoking their operations does not establish successful admission or creation, or the current viewer’s permission.

Optional `createOn` requires creation to be enabled and rejects a `cross-embedded` relationship. Its `on` must be `initialized` or `state`. `initialized` connects an automatic workflow to `Clauses Initialized`; `state` connects it to updates at `createOn/path`, with each step checking the current value against `createOn/equals`. The workflow calls `prepare` and then `create` with empty inputs and `automatic: true`; ordinary operations receive `automatic: false`. The planner establishes these triggers, not a guarantee of a completed attachment.

## Authority and access operations

`addAuthority_<clauseKey>` targets the configured authority and accepts `replacement`, which must include `lead/channel`. It requires `call/requireExactDocumentVersion` to be exactly `true`, an unfrozen roster, and `call/channel` to name a current party lead. An existing authority can be managed only through its own party channel; adding a missing authority also requires `allowNewParties`.

The operation validates party and representative names, checks participant access for the proposed roster and rejects conflicts with unrelated contract names. It adds generated roster contracts, replaces the authority party, clears `approved`, adds a newly introduced authority to `required`, increments `revision` from its source fallback of `1`, delegates activation-state computation and appends `Party Changed` with `party` and `revision`. The resulting active status depends on that activation computation.

`registerAccess_<clauseKey>` requires exact-version review, a current party-lead channel, an unfrozen roster and `allowNewParties`. Its `documents` contains one to sixteen Timeline Access publications. Each must have a Public Timeline Channel at `contracts/provider`, an initialized document and provider checkpoint history.

New registration stores references under `/attachmentAccess_<clauseKey>`, appends their paths to `/activation/accessPaths`, adds provider channels and refresh handlers, and returns `outcome: "acceptedNew"`. Existing registration returns `outcome: "duplicate"` only when the count and ordered publication identities match; different re-registration is rejected. The generated operation subsequently calls activation `refresh`, including after a duplicate result. Registration itself does not modify the publications’ permission sets or establish that all participant access is valid.

## Inherited checks

`checkRoster` requires a nonempty parent roster, every parent role in the child, and no additional child role except the configured authority. The authority must appear in the child and, for a cross relationship, in the parent. `samePrimary` requires matching `lead/channel` identities and equal, nonempty, duplicate-free `readerKeys` sets; ordering is immaterial. `origin(document)` requires `contracts/initialized/document` and returns its identity.

`accessValid` combines additional `readers` groups with party and representative `readerKeys`. External Channel transports bypass its access-document matching. Each Timeline Channel transport needs a matching Timeline Access document with the same provider and timeline and at least one allowed key from every reader group. Unsupported transport types and invalid access-document types reject the check; otherwise missing coverage returns `false`.

`requireCaller()` requires exact-version review and calls `requireActive` for `call/channel` with `workflow: true`. When `/activation` exists, this requires an active flag, valid participant access and a channel naming a current party or `<role>__<representative>`; when `/activation` is absent, `requireActive` skips those checks. These helper guards are not calls made by `plan()` itself.

`businessReady()` returns `true` when `/activation` is absent. Otherwise it requires the document not to be closed, all roles in `required` to be approved, every recorded `/activation/terms/fields` value to remain equal to its document value, and valid participant access. This helper’s result is distinct from the stored `active` flag.
